related_questions.question: Can you still catch COVID after being vaccinated?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, it is still possible to get COVID-19 even after being vaccinated. While the vaccines are highly effective, they do not provide 100% protection, and breakthrough infections can occur. However, vaccinated individuals are less likely to experience severe illness, hospitalization, or death compared to those who are unvaccinated.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, it is still possible to get COVID-19 even after being vaccinated

list.title: Breakthrough Infections:
list.snippet: Vaccinated individuals can still contract COVID-19, and this is known as a breakthrough infection.

list.title: Reduced Severity:
list.snippet: Studies have shown that vaccinated individuals who experience breakthrough infections tend to have milder symptoms and a lower risk of severe illness, hospitalization, or death compared to unvaccinated individuals with COVID-19.

list.title: Ongoing Protection:
list.snippet: The COVID-19 vaccines offer significant protection against severe illness and complications, but they do not eliminate the risk of infection entirely.

list.title: Importance of Vaccination:
list.snippet: Vaccination remains the best way to protect yourself and others from the severe consequences of COVID-19, including hospitalization and death.

list.title: Potential Symptoms:
list.snippet: Symptoms of a breakthrough infection may include fever, fatigue, sore throat, dry cough, and loss of taste or smell.

list.title: Importance of Continued Precautions:
list.snippet: Even after vaccination, it's important to continue practicing preventative measures like mask-wearing, social distancing, and good hygiene, especially in high-risk settings or when interacting with vulnerable individuals.

related_questions.title: Vaccine efficacy, effectiveness and protection

related_questions.question: How effective is the COVID vaccine at preventing infection?

text_blocks.snippet: The 2023-2024 COVID-19 vaccines are effective at reducing the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death from COVID-19, with a roughly 70% reduction in the risk of critical illness in the first two months after vaccination. However, the effectiveness of the vaccine in preventing infection specifically can vary and tends to decrease over time. While the vaccines provide substantial protection against severe outcomes, they don't guarantee complete prevention of infection.

list.title: Variant-specific effectiveness:

list.title: Importance of updated vaccines:
